parts.text:
11 A thin horizontal plate of area 0.036 m2 is beneath the surface of a liquid of density 930 kg m–3.
The force on one side of the plate due to the pressure of the liquid is 290 N.
What is the depth of the plate beneath the surface of the liquid?
A
0.88 m
B
1.1 m
C
1.8 m
D
8.7 m

hints: First use the $290 \text{ N}$ force on one side of the $0.036 \text{ m}^2$ plate to find the liquid pressure at that level using $p = F/A$.
Next connect that pressure to depth in the $930 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ liquid using hydrostatic pressure $p = \rho g h$.
Rearrange to $h = F/(A \rho g)$ and substitute $F = 290 \text{ N}$, $A = 0.036 \text{ m}^2$ and $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ to compare with the listed depths.
walkthrough: Find the pressure on the plate from the given force and area: $p = F/A$.
Substitute $F = 290 \text{ N}$ and $A = 0.036 \text{ m}^2$ to get $p = 290/0.036 \approx 8060 \text{ Pa}$.
State the hydrostatic pressure rule for depth $h$ in liquid of density $\rho$: $p = \rho g h$.
Rearrange for depth: $h = p/(\rho g) = F/(A \rho g)$.
Substitute $p \approx 8060 \text{ Pa}$, $\rho = 930 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$: $h \approx 8060/(930 \times 9.81) \approx 0.88 \text{ m}$.
Check units give $\text{N m}^{-2}/(\text{kg m}^{-3} \times \text{m s}^{-2}) = \text{m}$ with sensible precision for the data. This is option A.

A.explanation: Gives $h = 0.88 \text{ m}$ from $F/A = \rho g h$, which matches the pressure from $290 \text{ N}$ on $0.036 \text{ m}^2$.

B.explanation: Too large because it does not satisfy $290/(0.036 \times 930 \times 9.81)$ and overestimates the depth.

C.explanation: About twice the correct depth, possibly from an error in dividing force by area or omitting $g$ correctly.

D.explanation: Much too large, close to $F/(\rho A)$ without dividing by $g$, so it confuses mass with weight.
